newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended lower across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Friday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.85/98.90 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.92/98.97, September 2001 at S$97.80/97.85 against S$97.85/97.90 and June 2003 at S$95.80/95.85 from S$95.85/95.90.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2 1-7/8 versus Thursday's 1-3/8 1-1/4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.03/0.98 percent against Thursday's yield of 0.85/0.80 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.68/1.63 against 1.45/1.40 percent.
